title: Pricing & Packaging — back-of-envelope notes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for pricing/packaging ideas. Not a decision doc. Lots of TODOs, questions, and rough arithmetic.

Context + goals:
- Need simple public tiers for hosted API (free dev tier, standard, business) + enterprise/dedicated quoting.
- Goal: clear unit economics (per-token margin) and simple story to explain tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality).
- Also think about Dedicated reserved pricing (commit model) and burst/overage.

Assumptions (rough):
- GPU cost baseline: assume amortized inference infra cost ~ $2.50 / GPU-hour for on-demand hosted (including infra + ops + licenses). (placeholder)
- Throughput: a single GPU instance (A100/48GB equiv) forwards ~ 100 tokens/sec averaged across diverse workloads (our optimized runtime). For conservative math use 60 tps.
- Effective tokens per request: interactive chat avg 150 tokens (prompt+response). Batch/embedding flows different.
- Cost of S3 storage, logs, observability, infra adj: add 20% overhead to token compute cost.
- Desired gross margin target for hosted: 60-70% after infra & ops.

Token math (hosted API) — compute-driven cost per token:
1) GPU-second per token = 1 / tps. If tps = 60 tokens/sec -> 0.0167 sec/token.
2) GPU-hour cost $2.50 -> $2.50 / 3600 sec = $0.0006944 / sec.
   => compute cost / token = 0.0167 * 0.0006944 ≈ $0.0000116/token ~ 0.00116 cents/token.
3) Add 20% infra+ops overhead => $0.000014/token.
4) Add monitoring/analytics/license at scale (~0.000006/token) => total cost ~ $0.000020/token (2e-05).

Check sanity: At 1M tokens -> cost = $20. At 100M tokens -> $2,000.
If we price standard tier at $0.00008/token (0.008 cents) -> gross margin ~= (0.00008 - 0.00002)/0.00008 = 75% (nice).

Alternative tps assumptions: if tps = 100 -> cost/token compute drops to ~0.000007 => total ~0.00001. So margin improves. We should present a range in docs.

Embedding flows: cheaper per token? Actually embeddings are expensive model families but often shorter sequences; run per-request latency matters. E.g., embedding avg request size 100 tokens, throughput per GPU for embedding models might be 200 tps (higher). Rough cost per embedding request ~ $0.0005-0.001 (depends on model size). Need more concrete profiling.

Dedicated / Reserved pricing — back-of-envelope:
- Customer buys dedicated pool: e.g., 4 GPUs reserved. Pricing options: flat monthly fee per GPU (committed) or discounted usage rate.
- If cost to us per-GPU-month (amortized) = $2.50/hr * 24 * 30 ≈ $1,800/month (on-demand). With reserved instances, infra cost might be $1,200/month after commitments/discounts.
- Value-add: isolation, predictable throughput, priority routing, enhanced SLAs. We price markup target 2.5x-3x on infra to cover ops, support, SRE, account mgmt. => list price per GPU-month = $3k–$4k.
- For teams, sell per-pool pricing: e.g., small pool 4 GPUs = $12k/month (incl support), medium 8 GPUs = $24k/month. Add minimum commit term 3-12 months.

Bursting and overage:
- Offer burst tokens over committed capacity at premium (1.5-2x standard hosted rate) or let dedicated pools autoscale with metered pricing for burst.

Tier ideas (hosted API):
- Free (dev): 100k tokens/mo + rate limits, no SLAs, watermarked usage. Purpose: onboarding.
- Starter: $20/mo -> 250k tokens (simple monthly plan) -> effective price = $0.00008/token. Good for hobby/POC.
- Standard: $200/mo -> 3M tokens -> $0.000066/token. Discounts for annual commit.
- Business: $2k/mo -> 40M tokens -> $0.00005/token. Includes team seats, per-route dashboards, higher rate limits.
- Enterprise: custom quoting + Dedicated offering + support/SLA.

Notes on packaging levers:
- Rate limits (rps) are a lever to segment customers — Starter cheaper price but strict rps.
- Feature gates: streaming, long-context models, function-calling, higher concurrency only on paid tiers.
- Observability retention and evals as add-ons.
- Quantization/model-family: surface cheaper model variants (e.g., quantized 7B) as a lower-cost option for Standard; mark variation in pricing table and docs.

Unit economics sensitivity table (quick):
- Variables: tps, GPU-hour cost, overhead multiplier, price/token.
- Quick sensitivity: if GPU cost doubles (e.g., $5/hr) -> token cost doubles -> margins drop by ~50 percentage points. Mitigation: batching, KV cache, prefix caching, lowering avg tokens per request.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need empirical profiling across our model catalog: tps by model class (7B/13B/70B), avg tokens per request per product vertical.
- Confirm real infra cost per GPU-hour with finance (include networking, reserved discounts).
- Embedding model costs need separate profiling and potential per-embedding pricing (per-vector pricing).
- How to present pricing on website: per-token seems confusing to non-technical buyers. Consider "included tokens" per tier + overage price, and a per-1M token price in fine print.
- Decide whether to bill for prompt tokens and response tokens separately (we likely should count both).
- Draft examples for customers showing typical costs for chat bot (10k active MAUs, avg 5 calls/day, 150 tokens/call) -> run numbers and present.

Customer example (rough):
- 10k MAUs; 5 calls/day -> 50k calls/day -> 7.5M tokens/day (150 tokens/call) -> 225M tokens/month. At $0.00005/token -> $11,250/month. This would clearly push them to dedicated (cheaper at scale).

Messaging bullets for sales:
- "Predictable per-token pricing with clear committed discounts for teams that need predictable throughput."
- "Tiered plans for dev->production with seamless migration to Dedicated and Private deployments."
- "Optimize costs with model selection, quantization, and automatic caching — we surface these recommendations in Redwood Optimize."

References / links to flesh out later:
- profiling notes (confluence or infra runbooks) -> CONFLUENCE-12345
- Dedicated pricing comps (GCP/AWS marketplace listings) -> jira:PRIC-21

Random friction points to think about:
- Billing complexity (handle credits, refunds, overage disputes).
- Free-tier abuse -> need credit card verification or rate-limit heuristics.
- Enterprise negotiation: discounts vs commitments vs termination terms.

Next steps (my small checklist):
- [ ] Request GPU-hour / infra cost number from finance (assigned: Marco).
- [ ] Run microbench profiling for 7B/13B/70B to get tps baselines (assigned: eng-serving-runtime).
- [ ] Draft public pricing page prototype with simple tiers and per-1M token price (me).
- [ ] Create customer examples for web (low, med, high usage).
- [ ] Discuss dedicated pool packaging with sales (min pool size, support tiers).

Notes-to-self: keep the public-facing numbers simple. Use per-1M token easy math (e.g., $50 / 1M tokens) and then show how to optimize. Keep enterprise language flexible.

End of scratchpad. Many placeholders above — will iterate once we have profiling and finance numbers.
